body:
### Summary

### Summary

When a release has multiple wheels and only some of them are yanked (PEP 592 
per-file yanking, as opposed to yanking an entire release), `uv lock`/`uv sync` 
correctly avoid *selecting* the yanked wheel as the installed distribution, but 
the yanked wheel's URL and hash are still written into `uv.lock`'s `wheels` 
array for that package version. This happens regardless of which of the two 
wheels is the one marked yanked.

### Environment

- Index server: devpi, using the development releases that add per-file yank
  support:
  - `devpi-server==7.0.0b13`
    https://m.devpi.net/fschulze/dev/devpi-server/7.0.0b13
    (wheel: https://m.devpi.net/fschulze/dev/+f/a37/190b5b98e8f58/devpi_server-7.0.0b13-py3-none-any.whl)
  - `devpi-client==7.4.0.dev0`
    https://m.devpi.net/fschulze/dev/devpi-client/7.4.0.dev0
    (wheel: https://m.devpi.net/fschulze/dev/+f/62f/ee02e649fc647/devpi_client-7.4.0.dev0-py3-none-any.whl)
- Test registry: `http://127.0.0.1:8888/root/test`
- Package under test: `numpy==2.1.3`, two wheels for cp312/x86_64:
  - `numpy-2.1.3-0008fix-cp312-cp312-manylinux_2_27_x86_64.whl`
  - `numpy-2.1.3-cp312-cp312-manylinux_2_17_x86_64.manylinux2014_x86_64.whl`

### Repro

1. Using the devpi-server/devpi-client releases above (the first devpi versions
   to support yanking a single file within a release rather than the whole
   release), yank one wheel of `numpy==2.1.3` and leave the other unyanked.

2. Confirm via the index's simple API (both HTML and PEP 691 JSON) that exactly
   one of the two wheels carries `data-yanked` / `"yanked": "<reason>"`, e.g.:

```json
   {"filename": "numpy-2.1.3-cp312-cp312-manylinux_2_17_x86_64.manylinux2014_x86_64.whl",
    "yanked": "broken release", ...},
   {"filename": "numpy-2.1.3-0008fix-cp312-cp312-manylinux_2_27_x86_64.whl", ...}
```

3. `uv lock` (or `uv sync`) with `numpy>=2.1.3` as a dependency, pointed at that
   index.

4. Inspect `uv.lock`: **both** wheel entries appear under `[[package]] name = "numpy"`,
   including the yanked one, with its full URL and sha256 hash.

5. Reverse which wheel is yanked (unyank the manylinux_2_17 build, yank the
   0008fix build instead) and repeat. Result is symmetric: whichever wheel is
   yanked, it is still present in the regenerated lockfile.

### Why per-file yanking matters here, even though PyPI/Warehouse doesn't need it

PyPI conventionally yanks entire releases at once, so most tooling has only
ever had to reason about "is this whole version yanked." Private indexes that
build their own wheels hit a case Warehouse doesn't: a build for a given
version can fail or turn out broken for one platform tag, and the fix isn't a
new build number, it's a rebuild against a *different* manylinux tag (e.g. the
CI image gets bumped from `manylinux_2_17` to `manylinux_2_27`, or a build
picks up a newer/older glibc baseline). The wheel filename's build tag exists
to disambiguate multiple builds of the *same* platform tag; it has no way to
express "this replaces that other, differently-tagged wheel." Since the
version number can't be bumped either (nothing about the package's code
changed), yanking the specific broken file is the only mechanism available to
mark it unusable while leaving the version itself, and any lockfiles that
already pin to it via other still-good wheels, installable. Deleting the file
outright would break anyone who already resolved against that version; per-file
yanking is exactly the tool PEP 592 exists to provide for this. This is a new
capability in devpi as of `devpi-server` 7.0.0b13 / `devpi-client` 7.4.0.dev0
(linked above), so it's plausible no PEP 592 consumer has exercised this
specific partial-yank scenario against uv before.

### Root cause (as far as I can tell from the source)

- `crates/uv-resolver/src/version_map.rs` correctly computes per-file
  `WheelCompatibility::Incompatible(IncompatibleWheel::Yanked(...))` for a
  yanked file when a version is only partially yanked (comment there explicitly
  acknowledges this PEP 592 edge case).
- However, `PrioritizedDist::built_dist()` in
  `crates/uv-distribution-types/src/prioritized_distribution.rs` only strips
  wheels from the list it hands back (which ultimately becomes `uv.lock`'s
  `wheels` array) via `WheelCompatibility::is_excluded()`:

```rust
  fn is_excluded(&self) -> bool {
      matches!(self, Self::Incompatible(IncompatibleWheel::ExcludeNewer(_)))
  }
```

  This matches `ExcludeNewer` but not `Yanked`, so a yanked-but-not-selected
  wheel survives into the lockfile's wheel list even though it's correctly
  excluded from being the *installed* (`best_wheel_index`) wheel.

### Why this must be fixed at lock time, not install time

I traced this further and confirmed the fix genuinely has to happen when
`uv.lock` is written, there's no later point in the flow where a stale/yanked
entry could still be filtered out:

- The `Wheel` struct persisted into `uv.lock`
  (`crates/uv-resolver/src/lock/mod.rs`) has **no `yanked` field at all**. Once
  a wheel's URL/hash is written into the lock, all information about its yank
  status is gone.
- `uv sync --frozen` reads the lockfile and installs from it directly, with
  zero network calls for metadata (per `LockMode::Frozen` in
  `crates/uv/src/commands/project/lock.rs`, "*don't attempt to lock the
  project*"). It cannot re-check yank status even in principle.
- Plain `uv sync` only re-resolves if the lockfile looks stale relative to
  `pyproject.toml`'s constraints; a file being yanked after the fact isn't one
  of the triggers uv checks for; per uv's own docs, "*uv will not consider
  lockfiles outdated when new versions of packages are released*", the same
  applies here.
- Even `uv sync --locked`, which does force a fresh resolution to validate
  the lock, only errors if the *result differs*. Because of this bug, a fresh
  resolution against the same index state produces the same (still-including-
  the-yanked-file) wheel list, so it reports "unchanged" and proceeds to
  install from the old, yank-blind data anyway.
- At actual install time, `Package::to_dist()` picks the best wheel purely by
  platform tag (`find_best_wheel(tag_policy)`) against the statically stored
  wheel list; since that list carries no yank data, this step is structurally
  incapable of excluding a yanked file even if it wanted to.

In other words, the wheel-list-at-lock-time is the *only* place in uv's
pipeline where yank status is ever known and could be acted on. If a yanked
file isn't stripped there, it can never be stripped, which means every
downstream consumer of that lockfile (`--frozen` deploys, CI installs,
`uv export`) is permanently stuck referencing a file the index owner
explicitly marked broken, with no way to recover short of manually editing or
regenerating the lockfile from scratch.

### Suggested fix

Either broaden `is_excluded()` (and the analogous `SourceDistCompatibility::is_excluded()`)
to also match `Yanked(_)`, or add an explicit yanked-filter step in `built_dist()`
(and `source_dist()`, which has the same unconditional-inclusion pattern) before
the wheels are handed off to lockfile serialization. Presumably a yanked wheel
should still be kept if it is the *only* available wheel for a given marker/
platform combination (per the spec's carve-out), so the filter should probably
mirror the "is this the only option" logic already used for `AllowedYanks`
rather than a blanket drop.

### Platform

x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu

### Version

0.12.4

### Python version

3.12.13
title: Yanked wheel is retained in `uv.lock` even when a non-yanked wheel exists for the same version
